title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
1. Just bought a new computer and I am using it as an excuse to finally move entirely off Windows, so I am setting up Arch and figuring out how to get games working and all that.

    1. My Framework laptop should be arriving this week (if it can clear customs :'( ) and I'm hoping to finally give NixOS a shot. Good luck!

  2. Trying to find Europe-based partnerships for Uruky and investors for a different product (not under the same company because it'll require machine learning), which needs a good amount of cash investment upfront. Also trying to find some part-time work to help fund the lack of a paying job.

  3. Inspired by previous comments, was working on a new kind of terminal:

    • Screenshot: a top-like program running in the terminal.
    • Screenshot: filtering an object

    Programs output one of two binary formats, one being pure structured object data based on CBOR and the other being a kind of XML markup (the latter is what you see in the top screenshot: charts and a table nested within flex layouts). Then end goal is a PowerShell/nushell-like environment where external programs, not just builtin commands, can output structured data and, uh, nicely formatted markdown documents without resorting to sixels or custom terminal protocols for things like drawing borders on cells.

    Still a lot to work out, but I'm hoping to have a writeup soon which I might post here.

    1. I was thinking about something similar for a while, i will definitely read your writeup :D

    2. I'm getting 404s on those screenshots

  4. I am working on a PDF-merging program. This is to merge several pages from different PDF-files into one big page (not just concatenating the pages after each other). This is to align several maps produced from AutoCAD into one big map while removing overlapping sections.

    While it's a small project I have learned some new things already about MuPDF and I'm using Raylib for the simple UI.

    1. Working with PDFs like that is both a hassle and fun in a way for me. I’ve got a little script I knocked together at some point that takes 5.5x8.5in half-page PDFs as input and imposes them in the right order on 8.5x11in paper so that I can print on regular paper and make a single slice through the stack. It was a little tricky figuring out the right sequence, but not bad overall. We use it for making flight test cards and it’s saved me and my colleagues a surprising amount of hassle.

      1. Agreed. The file format is being used beyond its actual capabilities all over the place. Honestly I think the spec is not as unapproachable as the internet made it seem to me. We are a little limited on the ecosystem side, there are too few options (especially for rasterization/rendering) but still with the libraries we have, tooling around PDFs could be much better than its current state.

  5. Working to perfect mddog, a terminal tool that lets you preview Markdown in the terminal as if you're on GitHub or Obsidian: headings at the correct sizes, images rendered, etc.

    I look at Markdown files a lot for work and prefer to just stay inside the terminal without switching out of it so this has been a game changer.

    It basically works by building out the Markdown into its real format using macOS built-in engines like CoreText and CoreGraphics, then send the outputs to the terminal as image strips. I'm enjoying learning about the terminal, Rust, and the kitty graphics protocol throughout this process.

    If you give it a try, let me know how you like it!

    1. Coincidentally, I was working on a similar scenario recently: I wanted to convert all Markdown files in a repo to HTML, preserving links between Markdown files (as well as to other resources), for later viewing in a terminal browser (like w3m). I had gotten tired of piping cmark-gfm into w3m, and I've now got a 500 KB self-contained proof-of-concept (I actually just hacked it into my luasmith static site generator).

      The most similar tools I found prior to starting were grip (which depends on a GitHub endpoint) and Ghore (which is built on Node, which I've been successfully avoiding lately).

      mddog looks nice and is much fancier, but I needed to support older terminal emulators... and NetBSD :)

      1. I love when people's pain points coincide. I'll need to look at grip and Ghore -- they both sound like interesting projects. Good lock with building out your solution! Curious to see it if/when it goes public.

        I intentionally narrowed mddog to macOS and newer terminal emulators to ensure its fundamentals are well thought out and work properly first. Thinking about expanding its support down the line...but we'll see.

  6. I've been working on etoku, my Japanese language learning platform.

    The idea is that it tracks your understanding of the language per concept (vocabulary word or grammar point) and feeds you sentences from real TV and movies that review those or teach you one new concept. Right now I'm refining the system for choosing review sentences because I find it picks sentences that are optimal (review as many concepts at once as possible), but are too challenging, especially for users who don't know a ton.

    If you want to talk about language learning let me know at will@<the domain I linked to>! I love talking about this stuff.

  7. This week I'm promoting WordJoy, a Chinese character-building puzzle roguelike.

  8. Making progress on our job search! Qualified for a special program for finding temp work and already have one prospect in the queue.

    Played Magic: The Gathering for the first time in probably years. We can't recall playing since before Commander format came out and certainly hadn't bought any cards since then, not until tonight (pre-constructed Terra deck for the FFVI nostalgia).

    Off to New Anthrodam this weekend!

  9. I've been building a DST platform (similar to Antithesis) and I'm onboarding a couple of friends so they can test their own systems.

    1. I'd be quite interested in reading articles about your experience building it and "key takeaways" if you write it someday!

      1. I started writing one about how (deterministic) hypervisors work a couple of days ago. I will publish it soon!

    • Retaking my radio amateur exam... I almost passed the first time, aced 4 out of 5 sections, but alas the legal part tripped me up. I'm confident this time I'll have no issue.
    • Fighting an e-mail battle to return a faulty solar battery, that kept shutting itself down with an emergency error about voltage overloads. It's been three months since I opened my case and the company is really drawing things out.
    • At work I'm plugging holes. LLMs are relentless in finding issues.

  11. Small stuff at work since I'll be at OSMC for the next few days.

    I like events, but I'm a nervous "leaver" for travels. If I'm on the way I'm generally OK, but I always stress the leaving part :D

  12. Working with Nordic Thingy-91s. Power profiling with modern batteries is definitely a black magic (to me).

  13. Work: AI context layer management/ontology management for shared knowledge layers

    Home: building an axe throwing target

  14. I am having fun learning F* - although I wish it had a more Googleable name. Also in a rabbit hole about the Neolithic.

  15. Building a few things, spec'ing a few others. Trying not to burn out, and trying to navigate the extremely complicated political landscape that is modern working and wondering if I'll ever move beyond my current title even though I'm doing way more than my job description.

  16. I am working on rigorously testing my AI testing skill for Rails apps that I am launching next week.

    It's loosely based on my free testing guide https://minitestrails.com/ and it's sales will help me in sustaining the guide for a while.

  17. Been playing a lot of League of Legends. I used to think I was a gifted programmer, but after spending all my programming time playing league the past few months I've realized that it's probably just a result of me spending a lot of time programming. I thought that programming was what I was meant to do with my life, so I did it a lot and got good at it.

    Now that programming is dead and I've freed up my time for gaming, I've finally gotten decent at that. I hit Diamond rank, which is ~top 5%. I think that's probably close to or better than what I was as a programmer.

    It's nice to have video games as something where it still matters being good at something objective - doing something better than someone else. And for league at least, there's also some degree of reward for grind as well: you have to put in some effort and play a lot of games due to the inherent variance of a 5v5 competitive game. I think I still need to feel like I'm better than most other people at something in order to be happy, at this phase of my life.

  18. A place for long-form technical writing (mostly essays, not a blog), most likely going to be made with Astro.

• I am working on a PDF-merging program. This is to merge several pages from different PDF-files into one big page (not just concatenating the pages after each other). This is to align several maps produced from AutoCAD into one big map while removing overlapping sections.

    While it's a small project I have learned some new things already about MuPDF and I'm using Raylib for the simple UI.

    1. Working with PDFs like that is both a hassle and fun in a way for me. I’ve got a little script I knocked together at some point that takes 5.5x8.5in half-page PDFs as input and imposes them in the right order on 8.5x11in paper so that I can print on regular paper and make a single slice through the stack. It was a little tricky figuring out the right sequence, but not bad overall. We use it for making flight test cards and it’s saved me and my colleagues a surprising amount of hassle.

      1. Agreed. The file format is being used beyond its actual capabilities all over the place. Honestly I think the spec is not as unapproachable as the internet made it seem to me. We are a little limited on the ecosystem side, there are too few options (especially for rasterization/rendering) but still with the libraries we have, tooling around PDFs could be much better than its current state.

sentences.en: Working to perfect mddog, a terminal tool that lets you preview Markdown in the terminal as if you're on GitHub or Obsidian: headings at the correct sizes, images rendered, etc. I look at Markdown files a lot for work and prefer to just stay inside the terminal without switching out of it so this has been a game changer.
It basically works by building out the Markdown into its real format using macOS built-in engines like CoreText and CoreGraphics, then send the outputs to the terminal as image strips.
I'm enjoying learning about the terminal, Rust, and the kitty graphics protocol throughout this process.

• I've been working on etoku, my Japanese language learning platform.

    The idea is that it tracks your understanding of the language per concept (vocabulary word or grammar point) and feeds you sentences from real TV and movies that review those or teach you one new concept. Right now I'm refining the system for choosing review sentences because I find it picks sentences that are optimal (review as many concepts at once as possible), but are too challenging, especially for users who don't know a ton.

    If you want to talk about language learning let me know at will@<the domain I linked to>! I love talking about this stuff.

• Been playing a lot of League of Legends. I used to think I was a gifted programmer, but after spending all my programming time playing league the past few months I've realized that it's probably just a result of me spending a lot of time programming. I thought that programming was what I was meant to do with my life, so I did it a lot and got good at it.

    Now that programming is dead and I've freed up my time for gaming, I've finally gotten decent at that. I hit Diamond rank, which is ~top 5%. I think that's probably close to or better than what I was as a programmer.

    It's nice to have video games as something where it still matters being good at something objective - doing something better than someone else. And for league at least, there's also some degree of reward for grind as well: you have to put in some effort and play a lot of games due to the inherent variance of a 5v5 competitive game. I think I still need to feel like I'm better than most other people at something in order to be happy, at this phase of my life.

I was thinking about something similar for a while, i will definitely read your writeup :D I'm getting 404s on those screenshots
